'''Subhash Khot''' (born 10 June 1978 in [[Ichalkaranji]])<ref>{{Cite web |title=Subhash Khot - Heidelberg Laureate Forum |url=https://www.heidelberg-laureate-forum.org/laureate/subhash-khot.html |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=- Heidelberg Laureate Forum |language=en-EN}}</ref> is an [[Indian Americans|Indian-American]] [[mathematician]] and [[theoretical computer scientist]] who is the Julius Silver Professor of Computer Science in the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]]. Khot has contributed to the field of [[Computational complexity theory|computational complexity]], and is best known for his [[unique games conjecture]].<ref>{{citation
 | author-link = Subhash Khot
 | last = Khot | first = Subhash
 | contribution = On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games
 | doi = 10.1109/CCC.2002.1004334
 | title = Proceedings of the 17th Annual IEEE Conference on Computational Complexity
 | year = 2002
 | pages = 25| isbn = 978-0-7695-1468-0 | s2cid = 32966635 }}.</ref>

Khot received the 2014 [[Rolf Nevanlinna Prize]] by the [[International Mathematical Union]] and received the [[MacArthur Fellowship]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.macfound.org/fellows/960/ | title=Subhash Khot - MacArthur Foundation}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2017<ref>{{cite web |title=Subhash Khot |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/subhash-khot-13399/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523130226/https://royalsociety.org/people/subhash-khot-13399/ |archive-date=23 May 2017 |access-date=27 May 2017 |publisher=Royal Society}}</ref> and was inducted into the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News {{!}} NYU Courant |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1432/ |access-date=2023-08-27 |website=cims.nyu.edu}}</ref>

==Education==
Khot obtained his bachelor's degree in [[computer science]] from the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://alumni.acr.iitb.ac.in/awards/prof-subhash-khot-3/|title=Prof. Subhash Khot, B.Tech., 1999, Computer Science and Engineering|work=Alumni|publisher=IIT Bombay|access-date=2024-04-04}}</ref> He received his doctorate degree in computer science from [[Princeton University]] in 2003 under the supervision of [[Sanjeev Arora (computer scientist)|Sanjeev Arora]]. His doctoral dissertation was titled "New Techniques for Probabilistically Checkable Proofs and Inapproximability Results."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://awards.acm.org/doctoral_dissertation/year.cfm |title=ACM Doctoral Dissertation Award 2003 |access-date=2014-09-13 |archive-date=2014-11-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141103033017/http://awards.acm.org/doctoral_dissertation/year.cfm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Khot is a two time silver medallist representing India at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (1994 and 1995).<ref>{{IMO results|id=920}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Shirali | first1=S.A. | title=The Sierpinski problem  | year=2006 | journal=Resonance | volume=11 | issue=2 | pages=78–87 | doi=10.1007/BF02837277| s2cid=121269449 }}</ref> Khot topped the highly difficult IIT [[Joint Entrance Examination|JEE]] entrance exam in 1995.

He has been awarded the Microsoft Research New Faculty Fellowship Award (2005),<ref>[http://research.microsoft.com/en-us/collaboration/awards/msrff_all.aspx#2005 Microsoft Faculty Fellowship Recipients 2005]</ref> the [[Alan T. Waterman Award]] (2010), the [[Rolf Nevanlinna Prize]] for his work on the [[Unique Games Conjecture]] (2014), and the MacArthur Fellowship (2016).<ref>{{cite web|url =https://www.macfound.org/programs/fellows/strategy/ |archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20120402095519/http://www.macfound.org/programs/fellows/strategy/ |url-status =dead |archive-date =2012-04-02 |title =MacArthur Fellows Program}}</ref>

He was elected a fellow of the Royal Society in 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url= https://royalsociety.org/people/subhash-khot-13399/|title= Subhash Khot|publisher= Royal Society|access-date= 27 May 2017|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170523130226/https://royalsociety.org/people/subhash-khot-13399/|archive-date= 23 May 2017}}</ref> and was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News {{!}} NYU Courant |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1432/ |access-date=2023-08-27 |website=cims.nyu.edu}}</ref> In 2026, he received the Michael and Sheila Held Prize.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael and Sheila Held Prize |url=https://www.nasonline.org/award/michael-and-sheila-held-prize/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=30 June 2026}}</ref>
